topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing the topic of cancer therapy and stating the intended learning objectives.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and cytotoxic resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover traditional local and systemic interventions—including surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy—along with their associated toxicities and drug-efflux resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting cellular vulnerabilities and repair deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on selective treatment approaches that exploit cancer-specific vulnerabilities, including hormone receptor dependencies, cell cycle checkpoint losses, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Targeted kinase inhibitors and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the therapeutic targeting of hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and the molecular pathways driving resistance and drug addiction to kinase inhibitors.

topics.label: Antibody-based therapies and drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the use of monoclonal antibodies to directly target tumor surface antigens or selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads to cancer cells.

topics.label: Cancer immunotherapy and T-cell exploitation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine evidence for immune surveillance and strategies to engage host immunity through immune checkpoint blockade, bispecific T-cell engagers, and engineered CAR T cells.

topics.label: Therapeutic progress, future paradigms, and clinical dilemmas
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize historical trends in cancer survival against the challenges of tumor heterogeneity, biomarker-driven medicine, early detection, and the ethical dilemmas of clinical trial design.
